clue.text: Regularly furnish item of furniture that's wobbly

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word furnish, starting from its second

parts.note: a table is a common item of furniture

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture that rocks about, perhaps after being regularly furnished from a cheap shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' picks U, N, S from furnish; 'that's' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wobbly is unsteady and liable to tip, which is the plain dictionary sense.

clue.text: Positive aspect of promoted football team

parts.note: a promoted club goes up a division
a side is a team

explanation.surface: The good news for a football club that has just gone up a league.
explanation.definitionFit: The upside is the good or advantageous side of a situation.

clue.text: Cake makes tongue register

parts.note: Swiss taken loosely as a language, a tongue spoken in Switzerland
a roll is a list or register of names

explanation.surface: A dessert that leaves its mark on the taste buds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tongue' looks like the organ of taste; it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss roll is a rolled sponge with jam filling, a classic teatime treat.

clue.text: Film director's flared pants snag on part of gun

indicators.note: pants as slang for rubbish, so the letters of flared are made a mess of

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or problem
the cock is the hammer of a gun

explanation.surface: A director's bell-bottom trousers catch on a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers to go with flared; it is the anagram signal, British slang for poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Hitchcock directed thrillers such as Psycho and Vertigo.

clue.text: The French, extremely sycophantic, like opera house

parts.note: la is a French word for the

indicators.note: at the extremes, so the first and last letters of sycophantic

parts.note: a la means in the manner of, like

explanation.surface: A fawning French person gushing about a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: La Scala in Milan is one of the world's most famous venues for opera.

clue.text: Type of theatre doctor visits in the morning twice

indicators.note: a doctor who visits goes into the place, so these letters sit inside the others
the morning's abbreviation is written out two times over

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks the morning

explanation.surface: A doctor making house calls before noon, as it might be, then going off to the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: AM written twice gives AMAM, and 'visits in' puts DR into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Am-dram is short for amateur dramatics, a recognised kind of non-professional stage work.

clue.text: Female novelist organised trade crowd, spread at the front

indicators.note: the spread goes at the beginning, ahead of everything else

parts.note: marg is short for margarine, a spread

indicators.note: organised means the letters of trade are arranged anew

parts.note: a rabble is a disorderly crowd

explanation.surface: A writer organising a trade body, with butter substitute laid out first.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Drabble is an English writer known for The Millstone, among many other novels.

clue.text: Character in Marathon on Tyneside's a European runner

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and Marathon is in Greece
Tyneside lies in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: A Geordie athlete running a marathon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' looks like an athlete; rivers run. Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone flows through Switzerland and France, a river in Europe.

clue.text: One ignited in company of friend to fight for a cause

indicators.note: being in a mate's company puts these letters inside his

parts.note: a mate is a friend
one is the Roman numeral I
lit means set alight

explanation.surface: A lit torch is held in solidarity with a friend at a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: To militate is to campaign or work actively, often for or against something.

clue.text: Work on model's face

parts.note: OP, opus, is a musical work
to pose is what a model does, hence model as a verb

explanation.surface: A make-up artist working on a model's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face' seems a noun; it is the verb, to confront.
explanation.definitionFit: To face an opponent is to stand against them, the same as resisting.

clue.text: Formidable second row

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel, a row

explanation.surface: A rugby or theatre-seat description: the second row of the lineup is a formidable one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with cow here, a quarrel, not a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff opposition or a stiff test is hard to overcome, a familiar idiomatic sense of formidable.

clue.text: American turned through arch and left big sports event

indicators.note: turned round, so the short form for American is read backwards

parts.note: US stands for the United States, hence American
per means by way of or through, as in per post
a bow is a curve or arch shape

explanation.surface: An American spins round, passes under an arch and leaves for a big game.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the championship game of American football, one of the biggest annual sporting occasions.

clue.text: In emotionless situation, agents brought over old criminal

indicators.note: the agents are placed inside the word meaning emotionless, so this signals containment

parts.note: dead can mean without feeling, as in a dead voice

indicators.note: brought over means flipped round, so the word for agents is reversed

parts.note: reps, short for representatives, act as agents

explanation.surface: Undercover agents are shipped in to a lifeless situation to deal with a veteran crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' gives SPER, which 'In' places within; 'situation' is padding that rounds out the picture of being stuck in a lifeless place.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, especially of the Wild West, so a criminal by definition.

clue.text: Expert's appropriate clothing outside in deluge

indicators.note: clothing wraps round something, so the word for appropriate encloses the other letters

parts.note: apt means suitable or appropriate

indicators.note: the outside letters of deluge, its first and last

explanation.surface: Sensible rainwear worn out of doors in a downpour shows real expertise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside in deluge' gives D and E, which go inside APT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adept is highly skilled, a straightforward synonym for a master of a craft.

clue.text: Tease superior with a religious book

parts.note: to josh is to tease or kid someone
U, upper class, is the old label for socially superior usage

explanation.surface: Mocking someone of higher rank while carrying a holy text.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper class comes from the 1950s 'U and non-U' distinction in British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Joshua is a book of the Old Testament, so a religious book by example.

clue.text: View from east certainly popular

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
yes, as an emphatic certainly
something hot is in demand, popular

explanation.surface: A view from the east is certainly a popular one.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeshot is the range of one's sight, so whatever is within view.

clue.text: One might be in a stew, given tricky problem

definitions.text: One might be in a stew
definitions.meaning: a vegetable cooked hot in a casserole, taken literally
a contentious issue nobody wants to handle

explanation.surface: A worried person faced with a thorny issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a stew' tempts as 'agitated'; read literally it is the cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A burning issue that is passed quickly from hand to hand, like something too hot to hold.

clue.text: Relative keeping trim on runs gets minimal Chinese meal?

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the relative encloses the other letters

parts.note: a sib is a sibling, a relative
to pare is to trim
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A family member trims costs and eats a skimpy takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' marks a cryptic definition: spare as in meagre, plus a dish on Chinese menus.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare ribs are a staple of Chinese takeaways, while spare also means scanty.

clue.text: Artist might use this rented property within The Crown?

indicators.note: within puts the rented property inside the head-top word

parts.note: the crown of the head is the pate
a let is a property rented out

explanation.surface: A painter's question about a rented flat inside a pub called The Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Crown' looks like a pub or the monarchy; it is the top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter mixes colours on a flat board, the classic tool held while working at an easel.

clue.text: Repeatedly showing heart, helps Jason somewhere in Texas

indicators.note: the heart, all but the end letters, is taken from each of the two words in turn

explanation.surface: A generous man named Jason who keeps showing compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: El Paso is a city in western Texas, on the Mexican border.

clue.text: Grave site peripherally showing when person died, say

indicators.note: on the edges, so only the outer letters of site are used

parts.note: a date, for instance a date of death on a headstone

explanation.surface: A burial site whose headstone shows the date of death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like a noun in this cemetery scene; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and sedate both describe a calm, serious, dignified manner.

clue.text: Unhappy to involve doctor with the old dog

indicators.note: to involve means to take in, so the sorrowful word holds the others

parts.note: sad means unhappy
MO, medical officer, is a doctor
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: A miserable patient takes an old dog to see the vet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samoyed is a fluffy white Siberian breed of sled dog.

clue.text: Skill needed to include details in silver on shield?

indicators.note: include means to hold within, so the skill word wraps round the details

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
gen is slang for information or details

explanation.surface: A heraldic craftsman needing skill to engrave fine silver detail on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: Argent is the heraldic term for the silver tincture on a coat of arms.

clue.text: Pass priest leaving to deliver sermon

indicators.note: the priest leaves, so his letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: preaching is delivering a sermon

explanation.surface: A priest leaves the pulpit, passing on his duty to deliver the sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach someone something is to hand or pass it to them, as at a dinner table.

clue.text: Eagerly excited, Olga's opening in spades

parts.note: agog means eagerly expectant

indicators.note: the opening letter of the name Olga

explanation.surface: Olga is thrilled to open with a strong suit at bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in spades' suggests cards; here it means in abundance.
explanation.definitionFit: A gogo, from French, means in plenty, the same as having something in large quantities.

clue.text: Englishman abroad every year with dreary old hairstyle

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for an English person
PA, per annum, means each year
dour means gloomy or dreary

explanation.surface: A gloomy Brit living overseas sports the same dated haircut every year.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompadour is a swept-up hairdo named after Madame de Pompadour, popular in past centuries.

clue.text: Number ten, Lotus, crashed inside track without restraint

indicators.note: inside puts the figures and jumbled car name within the track letters

parts.note: RY, railway, is a track
ten written as digits 1 and 0, read as letters I and O

indicators.note: the car name Lotus is wrecked, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Car number ten, a Lotus, has crashed at the circuit after racing recklessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' makes TOUSL; Lotus is a British sports-car maker, which keeps the racing picture convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting riotously is acting wildly and unruly, with no restraint at all.

clue.text: Tone up, caber-tossing

indicators.note: tossing throws the letters of caber about

explanation.surface: Building muscle through the Highland Games sport of throwing a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Caber-tossing is a Scottish Highland Games event: hurling a long heavy pole end over end.
explanation.definitionFit: To brace is to tense or firm up the muscles, as in bracing oneself.

clue.text: War poet without money, without love

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the penniless word goes around the zero

parts.note: broke means penniless
love is zero in tennis, hence the letter O

explanation.surface: A soldier-poet left penniless and loveless.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'without' means outside: BROKE wraps O.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Brooke wrote The Soldier and other First World War poems.

clue.text: Gradually removed newsman, then another, putting in complaint

parts.note: ED, editor, is a newsman

indicators.note: the second editor is put into the word for the illness

parts.note: gout is a medical complaint
another newsman, so a second ED

explanation.surface: One newspaper editor ousts another after the rival's health complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To be edged out is to be eased out of a position bit by bit.
